answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable deposit before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm copied, fabricated, or mutually collusive output. Rewards accrue only after a task passes checks, and review assignments rotate with the tide so one cluster cannot reliably certify itself. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund many deposits and risk losing them; identities are not made impossible, but cheap disposable ones become costly. Saffron and basalt can serve as harmless task labels, not secret proof of personhood.
